subject: linear combination option in control compute?

messages.author: 828d260a55f62325
messages.subject: linear combination option in control compute?
parts:
Hi there, me again!

Checking some old documentation I found that a previous version of control.compute had the option (A=matrix)
so that it was possible that each observation could depend not only on one element of the latent Gaussian field but on linear combinations of elements of the latent Gaussian field. I see this is no longer the case! is it possible to do this?

Thanks

Karim

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] linear combination option in control compute?
parts:
On Tue, 2012-05-22 at 08:11 -0700, Karim Anaya wrote:
> Thanks! I did not express myself correctly!
>
>
> Is there anyway to the model which corresponds to the following data?
>

>
> as far as I understand, control.predictor(A=A) does not help!

yes! using this trick.

1. make the linear predictor equals each one of the component of the
model. so eta[1] = intercept, eta[2] = x1[1], eta[3] = x1[2], etc..,

2. build the model using the A-matrix.

here is your example; I think I got it correct.

******************

n = 3
m = 6
x1 = rnorm(m,mean=0,sd=1)
x2 = rnorm(n,mean=0,sd=1)
A = matrix(c(rep(1,6),c(1,0,1,0,1,0),c(0,1,0,1,0,1)),nrow=m,ncol=n)
y = 1+x1+A%*%x2


N = n + m + 1
intercept = c(1, rep(NA, N-1))
xx1 = c(NA, 1:m, rep(NA, N-(m+1)))
xx2 = c(NA, rep(NA, m), 1:n)

formula = y ~ -1 + intercept + f(xx1, model="iid") + f(xx2, model="iid")
AA = matrix(0, m, N)

AA[, 1] = 1
for(i in 1:m) {
AA[i, 1+i] = 1
}

for(i in 1:n) {
AA[, N-n+i] = A[, i]
}

r = inla(formula, data = list(y=y, xx1=xx1, xx2=xx2),
control.predictor = list(A=AA))
